newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power firm on heat, outages.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Mid-Atlantic spot power firm on heat, outages.

text.p: Spot electricity prices in the U.S. Mid-Atlantic territory were flat to higher Friday on lingering muggy weather and outages of nuclear plants in the region, industry sources said.
The effect of Tropical Storm Fran moving further inland was discounted by most who trade in the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland Interconnect (PJM) power pool.
"It'll miss PJM and hit the Great Lakes," said one PJM utility trader.
Three PJM nuclear power plants, with a combined capacity of 2,800 megawatts (MW), would be shut by next week.

General Public Utilities Corp's 610 MW Oyster Creek nuclear plant in Forked River, N.J., was shut Wednesday because of of condensor system problem, and was expected to remain shut for a 45-day maintenance program.
Pennsylvania Power and Light Co's 1,090 MW Susquehanna 1 nuclear unit in Berwick, Pa., was planned to be idled late today and to resume operation after 37 days from refueling.
PECO Energy Co scheduled to take its 1,100 MW Peachbottom 2 nuclear unit in Delta, Pa., off line on Friday, Sept 13 for roughly 29 days for refueling and maintenance.
"We're coming into a big maintenace season," said the PJM trader.
PJM firm, peak electricity prices were assessed at $21.00 per megawatt (MWh) for Saturday; $19.50 for Sunday; and $26.00-$27.00 for Monday, compared with the $24.00-$25.50 range from Thursday.
PJM firm, peak electricity for the five business days next week was discussed at $22.50-$23.50, up from Thursday's range of $22.50-$22.75.
Peak power for firm, peak delivery for rest of September was valued at $22.00-$22.20, flat from Thursday's level.
October PJM power, with similar delivery terms, was pegged at $20.50-$20.70, compared with Thursday's $20.50-$20.75.
November PJM electricity was again quoted in $21.50-$21.70 range, and December PJM at $22.40-$22.80.
Peak, firm PJM prices for the 1996 fourth quarter was assessed at $22.50-$22.75, unchanged from Thursday.
